Body Broken
bŏd´y brō´k'n
n. phrase (Christ's body given in death, as declared over the bread at the Supper; rendering Greek to soma to huper humon klomenon)
Broken, Old English brecan. The Greek klao is the ordinary verb for breaking bread, and the Authorized Version keeps the reading broken for you in Paul's account of the institution.

Biblical Definition

“And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me” (1Co 11:24); “This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me” (Luk 22:19). The breaking of the bread is the sign, and the communion is real: “The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?” (1Co 10:16). Isaiah had said what would be done to that body: “he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities” (Isa 53:5). And John records what was not done to it: “A bone of him shall not be broken” (John 19:36).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines break as to part or divide by force and violence; to burst; to rend apart; and, in the sacrament, the breaking of bread as the memorial of Christ's body.

expand to see more

BREAK, v.t. To part or divide by force and violence, as a solid substance.

2. To burst or open by force.

3. To rend; to tear; to part by piercing or penetrating.

4. To crush; to shatter.

BREAKING OF BREAD, in Scripture, the celebration of the Lord's supper.

Key Scripture

1Co 11:24 — "And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me."

Luk 22:19 — "And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me."

1Co 10:16 — "The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?"

Isa 53:5 — "But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed."

John 19:36 — "For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken."

Modern Corruption

The broken body is treated as a picture only, and the same Scripture that says broken for you says a bone of him shall not be broken.

expand to see more

Two sentences sit close together in the New Testament and look like a contradiction. Paul records the Lord saying this is my body, which is broken for you; John records that the soldiers, finding Him already dead, brake not his legs, and says it happened that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. Both are exact and neither yields. The body was broken in every way a body can be — scourged, pierced, bruised for our iniquities — and the passover lamb's one structural requirement was kept to the letter, so that the sign and the substance agreed even in the manner of the death. What was broken was the man; what was not broken was the lamb.

The corruption on one side makes the bread the body in substance, so that the breaking is a re-breaking; the corruption on the other empties it entirely, so that the bread is a visual aid and the table a lecture with props. First Corinthians 10:16 refuses both by calling it a communion of the body of Christ — a real participation, in which believing receivers feed spiritually on a Christ who is bodily in heaven and truly given to them by the Spirit. The Confession's phrase is that they receive and feed upon Christ crucified, really and indeed, yet not carnally and corporally, but spiritually.

The most neglected word in the sentence is for you. The breaking is not presented as a fact to be admired at a distance but as a transaction with a beneficiary named, and the command that follows is not to analyse it but to remember: this do in remembrance of me. Paul adds the warning that a man may eat unworthily and be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, which would be an extravagant thing to say about a symbol and is a sober thing to say about a communion.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek klao (G2806), to break, of bread; soma (G4983), body; koinonia (G2842), communion, participation; anamnesis (G364), remembrance; suntribo (G4937), to break in pieces.

expand to see more

Greek klao (G2806) — to break bread; 1 Corinthians 11:24, 10:16, Matthew 26:26, Acts 2:46, 20:7.

Greek koinonia (G2842) — communion, participation; 1 Corinthians 10:16, 1:9, 2 Corinthians 13:14.

Greek suntribo (G4937) — to break in pieces; John 19:36, quoting Exodus 12:46, Psalm 34:20.

Usage

"“This is my body, which is broken for you” — a transaction with a beneficiary named."

"“A bone of him shall not be broken” — the lamb's one requirement, kept."

"“The communion of the body of Christ” — more than a symbol, less than a substance."
